attributes.board_name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Medicine

rules.accepted_credit_types: Category 1 or 2 (CME Pilot Program, Policy 17-05); Category 1 from ACCME, AOA, AAFP or ACCME-recognized state medical society providers (AMA PRA Category 1, AAFP Prescribed, AOA 1-A); most credits should relate to the licensee's area of practice
rules.new_licensee_rule: Licenses renewing within one year need no CME; renewal period between one and two years requires half of the biennial requirement. One-time trainings (child abuse, domestic/sexual violence, EHR, implicit bias) are required at initial licensure.
rules.alternatives: Exempt: limited licensees, inactive status, residents/fellows in ACGME/AOA programs, first two years of non-accredited fellowships, military called to service in a national emergency. Partial waiver on request at least 30 days before renewal.
rules.audit_note: Board says it is not currently running random CME audits (only linked to investigations). Keep CME records at least one full renewal cycle after earning them.

topics.who: Licensees who prescribe controlled substances (opioid education and pain management; may count toward risk management)
Risk management study (patient safety, error prevention, ethics, medical-legal issues etc.); up to 7 credits in physician wellness/burnout may count
Reading the Board regulations 243 CMR 1.00-3.00 (counts as 2 credits)
Physicians serving adult populations: Alzheimer's disease and related dementias
Recognizing and reporting suspected child abuse and neglect (mandated reporter training)
Domestic violence and sexual violence training; only a DPH-approved course counts

rules.notes: One board licenses MDs and DOs. 243 CMR 2.06 still states 100 credits (40 Cat 1); since 2018 the Board's CME Pilot Program (Policy 17-05) requires 50 Cat 1 or 2. One-time: 3 credits EHR proficiency (unless proficient/waived).
rules.legal_basis: 243 CMR 2.06; M.G.L. c. 112, §2; Board Policy 17-05 (CME Pilot Program)
